problem: Prior embodied multi-agent cooperation work (CoELA, CaPo) operates in small, mostly static indoor scenes where simple obstacle avoidance suffices, and does not address city-scale outdoor coordination under dynamic hazards, partial knowledge and coarse map tools.
motivation: Humans agree on safe, convenient meeting points in a city by sharing updates and replanning around hazards using a coarse map. Scaling embodied cooperation to this needs spatially grounded memory, communication and replanning, which existing LLM agents lacking spatial modules do poorly.
key_idea: CoSaR gives decentralized LLM/VLM agents a shared-by-communication spatial memory (occupancy map with danger zones, pose registry, ETA map, meeting plan) that drives a reasoner choosing query/communicate/navigate/wait, with VLM-based route refinement over an annotated map plus classical A* control.
insight: Spatial memory content, especially ETA map and known poses extracted from messages, matters most: removing the Message Analyzer or Spatial Memory drops success from 32.14 to 19.26 and 21.42, while removing route refinement or emergency avoidance drops it to 26.19 and 24.05. Route refinement by VLM is weak (only about 18-28% success) so gains come mostly from communication and memory; CoELA's low caught rate is due to staying idle at safe start locations, not safer navigation.
method: Perception Module: Grounding-DINO detection, SAM2 masks, depth projection to point clouds, CLIP features, voxel grid; sentinels matched by features and marked with warning labels
Communication Module: LLM extracts agent poses, sentinel poses, ETAs and teammate opinions from messages, checks agreement, and generates concise messages from the spatial memory
Spatial Memory: occupancy map with danger zones (radius 10, hyperbolic-constraint labeling, cleared when observed safe), ETA map per agent per place, meeting plan with reference route
Spatial-aware Reasoning Module: zero-shot LLM chooses Query / Communicate / Navigate / Wait from memory and dialogue; triggered on new events, disagreement, or every 120 s

Route Refinement: when the map-tool route crosses danger zones, QueryMap image is annotated (route, danger zones) and a VLM proposes waypoints, validated by QueryRefinedRoute, with fallback to removing danger-zone waypoints after N retries
Emergency Avoidance: on warning signal or sentinel within 40 m, move 10 steps to a sampled target away from sentinels, then rescan
Low-level control: A* on the occupancy map following refined waypoints

setting.backbone: gpt-4o (frozen) for reasoning, communication and route-refinement VLM; Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct variant; Grounding-DINO + SAM2 + CLIP for perception
setting.training_data: none (training-free); only the MAT baseline is trained with PPO
setting.observation: egocentric 512x512 RGB-D, natural-language messages from teammates, map tool outputs
setting.action_space: continuous navigation via A* over waypoints, plus communication and map-tool query actions (QueryRoute, QueryNearby, QueryPlace, QueryMap, QueryRefinedRoute)
setting.privileged: none for the main setting; an 'Oracle Perception' variant uses ground-truth segmentation; oracle baselines use GT agent positions

numbers.bench: other:Sentinel Challenge w/ Oracle Perception (5 agents, 10 stationary sentinels)
other:Sentinel Challenge w/ Oracle Perception (5 agents, 10 patrolling sentinels)
other:Sentinel Challenge (5 agents, 5 stationary sentinels, Qwen backbone)
numbers.eval_set_note: 14 scenes, 2 runs, oracle perception setting (matches gpt-4o row in Table 'Performance Comparison Across Foundation Model Backbones')

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmarks; only the paper's own Sentinel benchmark, which has no official split names ('test' used as placeholder). Additional settings (3 agents/10 sentinels, 5/5, 5/20) are in the appendix tables and Table 2 but not all listed here.
results: CoSaR achieves the highest success rate in most settings, e.g. 32.14% vs RoCo 26.19%, CoELA 16.67% and MAT 0.00% with 5 agents and 10 stationary sentinels, and 53.57% vs RoCo 46.43% with oracle perception. It generally has the lowest time cost, though on patrolling sentinels its caught/detection rates are not the best and absolute success remains low (mostly under 40%).
limitations: Absolute success rates remain low (about 20-55%) and caught rates are high, especially with patrolling sentinels and many sentinels
VLM route refinement has limited spatial reasoning, with only about 18-28% success
Evaluation limited to a single simulator/scene set with only 14 scenes, modest runs, and GPT-4o-based reasoning with high token and wall-clock cost
